headline: Spatial omics methods infer proteins, nuclei and cell identities across modalities and 3D
label: Spatial Multimodal Omics Inference
summary: Preprints and two journal papers extend cross-modal inference, from H&E to protein and RNA-guided morphology, alongside multi-omic integration and segmentation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is inferring one spatial measurement layer from another or aligning layers within a shared model. QUEST virtually stains H&E to multiplex immunofluorescence, and MorphoProt uses RNA-guided cross-attention over multiscale histology to predict spatial protein abundance. MAD conditionally edits nucleus images and CosMx gene expression, while CORAL and DIRAC integrate multi-omic and cross-study data with graph attention or domain adaptation. A second thread refines the cellular unit of quantification: Tracel reassigns transcripts by optimal transport, PixAQ attributes pixels per marker in imaging mass cytometry, and SSAF-T infers cell types without segmentation. THiRST extends the setting to 3D reconstruction from serial sections. The new element is conditioning across modalities and scales, rather than single-modality analysis.
